author: jue-henry
body:
Final approach we landed on:

1. find image records on mongo
2. utilize mongo transactions to delete the appropriate records:
- we delete all image records, image attempt records, and image error records each in their own respective operation instead of 1 per image per type of record
- if an error occurs we abort all changes to mongo and return with an error

3. if mongo records are successfully deleted, we then delete the corresponding s3 objects all at once

Note: We opted to delete mongo records first, and then delete s3 objects, since a record without an image is more detrimental than a image without records. Thought was put into ensuring both are there, but converting the mongo deletion record operation to use `deleteMany` instead of `deleteOne` makes it so that we have far less per image errors available.

### Description:

Updates the UI of the `BaseTextField` based on the new design. See the linked issue for the design document.

### Summary of changes:

- Removed trailing "Clear" and "Done" action icons for a multi line text field.
- Set min and max lines for multi line text fields.

author: sjoerd-bouma
body:
Based on #89 

Adds tests for `skip_incomplete=True` and also a first effort at a benchmark test - all workflow runs on `main` should store the time per event required for each configuration of backend/calibration etc, and the test will fail if a new branch increases the time on any of these by more than 50%.

It's not the tidiest code I've ever written and we can probably do something smarter but maybe this is good enough for now.

(As an aside - a consequence of benchmark data only being stored on `main` means that it doesn't actually compare anything yet, so we'll have to see if it works or not in due course :)

author: bdach
body:
As [pointed out internally](https://discord.com/channels/90072389919997952/983550677794050108/1306327452364177418).

- `plain/text` is exactly backwards; [it's actually `text/plain`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/MIME_types#textplain).
- The MIME type spec is redundant there anyways. [`StringContent` implicitly means `text/plain` by default until specified otherwise.](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.net.http.stringcontent.-ctor?view=net-8.0#system-net-http-stringcontent-ctor(system-string))
- And the only place that used the `StringContent` path was wrong anyway, it was supposed to be doing `application/x-www-form-urlencoded`. [Which `FormUrlEncodedContent` is for, and is now used in the relevant context.](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.net.http.formurlencodedcontent?view=net-8.0)

Mind you, all this seems to have absolutely no impact on anything whatsoever and be 100% academical, because as far as I can see, on local environment the web LIO endpoint just responds with 204 anyways, with or without this PR. I'd expect 415 if it didn't like anything above, so I'm wagering it just didn't care or check and all of this had an impact of exactly none whatsoever.

author: bukhtyarhaider
body:
### Pull Request: Improvements and New Functionality for Hostel Booking Process

#### Summary
This PR introduces enhancements to the **RequestDecisionModal** and **HostelRequestCard** components, as well as the addition and configuration of the **BookThisHostel** functions. These updates streamline the hostel booking process, improve UX/UI components, and add backend functionality for managing bookings and reservations.

#### Changes

1. **Improvements to RequestDecisionModal**:
   - Enhanced UI/UX for the modal to provide a clearer user experience when deciding on booking requests.
   - Improved responsiveness and accessibility for mobile and desktop views.
   - Refactored code to increase maintainability and efficiency.

2. **Enhancements to HostelRequestCard**:
   - Optimized layout and styling for better readability and interaction.
   - Added conditional rendering to display relevant booking details dynamically.
   - Improved component performance with refined state handling.

3. **Addition of BookThisHostel Functions**:
   - Added Firebase functions to handle hostel booking processes, including `makeReservation`, which checks room availability, decrements seat count upon booking, and retrieves warden information for the selected hostel.
   - Configured error handling for cases such as no available seats and missing data fields.
   - Updated booking application status to `"reserved"` once a reservation is confirmed.

#### Testing
- All new and updated components and functions were tested locally to ensure proper functionality.
- Verified that bookings are only made when rooms have available seats and that the status is updated accurately.
- Confirmed the modal and card components render and behave as expected across different devices and screen sizes.

#### Notes
This PR primarily focuses on the hostel booking functionality and component improvements. Future enhancements could include further UI refinements and unit tests for the new backend functions.

author: lahm86
body:
Resolves #1883.

#### Checklist

- [x] I have read the [coding conventions](https://github.com/LostArtefacts/TR1X/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#coding-conventions)
- [x] I have added a changelog entry about what my pull request accomplishes, or it is an internal change

#### Description

This follows a similar approach as we did for TR1 in #941. Best viewed commit-by-commit to see the iterative changes.

As well as the main FD overhaul, there were a few snagging points that have been addressed here.
- `Item_Initialise` was previously called during `M_LoadItems` in `level.c` but this had to be shifted because there are floor data dependencies there. We now take a similar approach to TR1, so load the level data, then perform a "CompleteSetup"; this can be expanded later for things like injection processing.
- With the above, @aredfan found that if you start a level then go back to the title screen, it can crash. `g_LevelItemCount` wasn't being set to 0 here - not an issue originally because `Item_Initialise` (where the crash would occur) would have been skipped in that case.
- While the triggers that are meant to activate after pulling the dagger from the dragon are heavy, the call to test triggers came from Lara's extra anim routine. As we now pass the item, which determines the heavy state, this had to be amended to locate the dragon bones item and to pass that. The dragon control has already ended by the time the extra anim completes so we couldn't add the call anywhere there, and running it too early meant issues like the camera still being in cinematic mode while looking at the doors opening.

The dragon may need some extra checks based on where it lands e.g. if partially in the wall. I may change this to behave like the Torso in TR1, where it checks a range of surrounding sectors.

For testing, attached is a level with various trigger types, basic geometry, ladders, and death tiles. I didn't include a dragon for testing, that can be done in OG easily enough. For ceiling geometry, it's best to fly against it and hold down to see that Lara follows the structure properly.

[WALL.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/17750165/WALL.zip)

There is a lot of scope now for sharing FD handling with TR1, but that can be tackled in the future. I may follow this up with some minor changes, like moving all FD macros to libtrx and renaming some enums, but I didn't want to touch TR1 at all in this PR.

author: nwalters512
body:
This ended up being a disaster in prod. `user_sessions` is referenced by `client_fingerprints`, which in turn is referenced by `assessment_instances`, `assessment_state_logs`, `page_view_logs`, `submissions`, and `variants`. That means that deleting a single `user_sessions` row would require table scans of all those tables; things only got worse when we tried to delete a _bunch_ of `user_sessions` rows.

Given that `user_sessions` is really meant to be somewhat ephemeral, I wonder if we should in fact be using _any_ foreign keys pointing into the `user_sessions` table. While I acknowledge that actual foreign key constraints are nice, maybe it's better to just treat `user_session` IDs as an opaque value in `client_fingerprints`. That's a question for another PR though.

body:
Description
-----------
<!--
Include reference to internal ticket "Fixes WB-NNNNN" and/or GitHub issue "Fixes #NNNN" (if applicable)
-->
- Fixes [WB-19117](https://wandb.atlassian.net/browse/WB-19117)

This PR adds support for downloading azure reference artifacts in core.

The core/vendor files can be ignored, they are autogenerated because of the new azure imports

Brief explanation of the azure clients setup:
There are 3 types of azure clients we use: account level clients, container level, and blob level clients.

account level clients: should mostly be shared across the manifest entries/tasks. we store these in a map of account url -> client. these can be used to download blobs given that they aren't versioned/we don't need to use a version to download them.
container level clients: this should also be mostly shared across the manifest entries/tasks. we use this only when we need to search for the correct version of a blob when the digest we have stored doesn't match the etag we get from naively searching.
blob level clients: this is unique to each manifest entry/task. this is used to confirm matching etags/digests and to download blobs if we have a version id.

NUnit Analyzers 4.14 - June 1, 2026

This release of the NUnit Analyzers adds a new analyzer and associated codefix - `NUnit2059` - that helps ensure that
async assertion methods in NUnit version 5 and higher - i.e. `Assert.ThrowsAsync`, `Assert.CatchAsync`, and
`Assert.DoesNotThrowAsync` - have their results observed, as these methods are awaitable from NUnit version 5.

The release contains contributions from the following users (in alphabetical order):

- [@​manfred-brands](https://redirect.github.com/manfred-brands)
- [@​mikkelbu](https://redirect.github.com/mikkelbu)

Features and Enhancements

`ActualValueDelegate<>` with `Func<>` - see [nunit/nunit#4824](https://redirect.github.com/nunit/nunit/issues/4824) for more information.
Analyzers now also consider the return type of `Func<>` in assertions. The release also includes one bug fix and
some dependency updates.

NUnit Analyzers 4.12 - March 3, 2026

This release of the NUnit Analyzers improves `NUnit1029` to account for `TestCaseSource`
support for params and optional arguments. It also introduces a new analyzer for incorrect
usage of `Is.Not.Null.Or.Empty`, fixes regressions in `NUnit2005` and `NUnit2055`, and updates
NUnit package dependencies.

Integrate ViewModel into EditProfileScreen

## Description
This PR introduces the integration of `UserViewModel` into `EditProfile` to handle loading and saving user data. It closes issue #163 .

## Changes
- Implemented `UserViewModel` into `EditProfileScreen` to use for loading user data.
-  Changed variables to manage user profile data.
- Implemented `UserViewModel` into `EditProfileScreen` to use for saving user data.
